topic: Annual leave is welcome. It is not a burnout strategy.
text:
Most teams are back from the summer break this week. Some will already feel like they never left. That isn't a failure of their leave.

In a large review of studies of healthy workers, wellbeing rose during a holiday and then eased back in the weeks after returning to work. These were not studies of people with burnout, but the pattern is worth noticing: leave helps, and the lift fades once work resumes.

That fits Australia's model Code of Practice on psychosocial hazards. It asks workplaces to aim first to eliminate risks such as high job demands, low job control and poor support, rather than relying on people to recover from them.

A useful question for any manager this month: what will people come back to?

Key sources:
Grant, R. S., Buchanan, B. E., & Shockley, K. M. (2025). I need a vacation: A meta-analysis of vacation and employee well-being. Journal of Applied Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001262
Safe Work Australia. (2022). Model Code of Practice: Managing psychosocial hazards at work. https://www.safeworkaustralia.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-08/model_code_of_practice_-_managing_psychosocial_hazards_at_work_25082022_0.pdf
